title: Vermont AI Laws

reading.body:
Vermont has enacted one AI-related law, and it governs synthetic media in elections rather than AI development, data centers, or compute.

The law, S0023, passed on 2026-03-10. It requires a disclosure on synthetic media that is deceptive and fraudulent when published, communicated, or distributed within 90 days before an election in Vermont. It sets format requirements for that disclosure in images, video, and audio, provides penalties for knowing and intentional violations, gives enforcement and investigation powers to the Attorney General and State's Attorneys, and allows candidates to seek injunctive relief.

For AI specifically, this is a narrow instrument. It reaches generated or altered media only near an election, only when the content is deceptive and fraudulent, and only when it is distributed in Vermont. It does not regulate model training, compute, data centers, or electricity, so it says nothing about the infrastructure constraints that shape AI scaling.

What the data does not cover is equally clear. One law is the entire Vermont record here, so no trend can be read from it. The text does not state how disclosure requirements will be verified, how synthetic media will be detected, or how the 90-day window interacts with media published outside Vermont. The count reflects laws this site judged relevant to AI, not every law that touches automated systems.
